clue.text: Sharp-edged USA shirt folds for one killed in the 28

parts.note: crisp means cleanly and sharply defined
taken as written
a T is a T-shirt
tucks are folds stitched into cloth

explanation.surface: A crisply ironed American shirt seems to be folded for a fallen soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: CRISPUS ATTUCKS, a sailor of African and Native American descent, was the first person shot in the 1770 Boston Massacre (28-Across).
explanation.definitionFit: Attucks is remembered as the first casualty of that 1770 clash between British soldiers and a Boston crowd.

clue.text: They clash, and it sounds like they stand for something

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the word is heard as another one, so go by sound

parts.note: symbols are signs that represent something else

explanation.surface: Things that conflict, yet are said to represent an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clash' suggests disagreement, but it is the crash of brass plates struck together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbals are percussion instruments played by striking them together with a ringing crash.

clue.text: Know-nothing featured in campaign (or a musical)

indicators.note: featured in says the letters appear within the following words

parts.note: running across campaIGN OR A MUSical

explanation.surface: An ignorant person appearing in a political campaign, or in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, someone who knows nothing.

clue.text: Weird Al's specialty punishment: interrupting compensation

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: pay is money given in compensation
the rod, a cane used for beating, stands for punishment

explanation.surface: A comedian's trademark: being punished by docked wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird Al' Yankovic is a US comic singer famous for spoof versions of pop hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a comic imitation of another work, the genre Weird Al Yankovic is known for.

clue.text: Mineo's a dip

parts.note: Sal Mineo was an American actor
the S and the A taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling the actor Mineo a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Sal Mineo starred in Rebel Without a Cause. 'Dip' reads as an insult (a dipstick), but it is the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy tomato sauce served as a dip for chips.

clue.text: Belatedly crept around slowly, say, with heads on a big stick

indicators.note: arriving late means missing the start, so the word lacks its first letter
around says one word goes about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: stole, meaning crept quietly, without its opening letter
slowly is an example of a tempo, the speed of music

explanation.surface: Someone crept about at a slow pace with heads stuck on a pole, like a grim procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crept' gives STOLE in its sense of moved stealthily; 'say' marks slowly as just one example of a tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a tall carved post bearing stacked faces and figures, made by Pacific Northwest peoples.

clue.text: Why, to run amok is contemptible

indicators.note: running amok means rampaging out of control, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declaring that running wild is despicable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run amok' reads as one phrase; 'run' is fodder and 'amok' alone the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Unworthy, in its sense of shameful or beneath one, is close to contemptible.

clue.text: Rise to go back through waterfall on Kilimanjaro

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end towards the start
through says the letters run right across the following words

parts.note: running across waterfaLL ON Kilimanjaro

explanation.surface: A climber heading back past a waterfall on the African mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'rise' also suggests reading upward, which fits the backwards reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A knoll is a small rounded hill, a rise in the ground.

clue.text: Aluminum found by one who goes underground, for example!

definitions.text: Aluminum found by one who goes underground, for example!

parts.note: a miner works below ground
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminum

explanation.surface: A miner digging underground comes across aluminum.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: aluminum ore is a mineral that a miner finds. The exclamation mark flags that double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminum is an example of a mineral, a natural substance that miners dig out of the ground.

clue.text: Line used for drawing to distort power

indicators.note: to distort something is to twist it out of shape, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist's drawn line seems to warp power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching with a pencil, but here it means pulling, as a vehicle draws a trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A towrope is a cable used to pull, or draw, a vehicle behind another.

clue.text: Communist that is traveling up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a red is a communist
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A Communist that travels about all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and down' reads as one idiom for back and forth, but 'down' is the definition: soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eider is a sea duck whose soft breast feathers give eiderdown, the original down for quilts.

clue.text: Harsh and dry, containing carbon

indicators.note: containing says one word holds another inside it

parts.note: arid means very dry
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Something harsh and dry with carbon in it, like smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a harsh, bitter smell or taste, and by extension a harsh manner.

clue.text: Carload Mr. Savage covered with protective layer

indicators.note: to savage is to maul and tear apart, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the title's two letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Savage has his car covered in a protective coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr. Savage' reads as a name (Doc Savage, Fred Savage), but Savage is a verb acting on the letters of 'Carload Mr.'
explanation.definitionFit: Armorclad means sheathed in armor, a protective covering of metal plates.

clue.text: Body of prophet from the East

indicators.note: coming from the East means reading from right to left, as a map puts east on the right

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: The remains of a prophet arriving from eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMA is the biological term for the body of an organism, as opposed to its germ cells or mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Soma is a technical word for the body, as in psychosomatic, from the Greek for body.

clue.text: Placate pushy type, restraining academic

indicators.note: restraining something means holding it in, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a shover is someone who pushes
academic and moot both mean of no practical relevance

explanation.surface: Calming down an aggressive person who is holding a professor back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic' looks like a scholar to be restrained, but it is the adjective, meaning merely theoretical.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth over a quarrel is to calm the parties and placate them, making the trouble seem less serious.

clue.text: Masculine role: to whip a cocktail

parts.note: a man is male
a hat is a role, as in wearing many hats
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A macho bartender's job: whisking up a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests whisking a cocktail; it is the beating sense, as in tanning someone's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a classic cocktail of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters.

clue.text: 6+3+51 Celsius — that's scathing

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a trio is a group of three
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals
C is the abbreviation for Celsius

explanation.surface: A sum adding up to a temperature hot enough to scald.
explanation.walkthrough: The plus signs look like arithmetic giving 60, but each number is turned into letters separately and joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic criticism is bitterly harsh, like the corrosive acid vitriol, so it is scathing.

clue.text: They measure your apartment and keep you out of the army

definitions.meaning: first meaning: units of length used to measure an apartment

definitions.text: keep you out of the army
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a foot condition that disqualified recruits

explanation.surface: Sounds like a riddle about officials who survey your home and grant draft exemptions.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat is the British word for apartment, so the first half is flat-feet, the measurements of a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet measure a flat, and fallen arches were long grounds for rejection from military service.

clue.text: Writer's jig snarled terribly…

indicators.note: something snarled is tangled into knots, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
this word does double duty as fodder; only its first letters are not used twice

explanation.surface: An author's dance has become badly tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: J. D. Salinger wrote The Catcher in the Rye. The ellipsis runs the surface into the next clue but the wordplay ends here.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger is a famous American novelist, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: Talked a lot — yes, in German — and then got married

parts.note: ja is German for yes
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: Someone chatted on, said yes in German, and then married.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is informal for chattering at length, so jawed means talked a lot.

clue.text: …on a spinner

parts.note: taken as written
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the author's jig is danced on a spinning toy.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis links the surface to 18-Across only; the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop and on are synonyms when saying where something rests: a hat atop a head.

clue.text: Criticize pine with flair

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticize it harshly
to pine for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A critic slating something about pine trees with style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree, but it is the verb meaning to long.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is stylish confidence and dash, which is what flair means.

clue.text: URL was tweaked to represent character from Lewis Carroll

indicators.note: something tweaked has been adjusted, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also does duty in the indicator

explanation.surface: A web address adjusted to stand for a figure from Alice's adventures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Walrus and the Carpenter is a poem recited in Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass.

clue.text: In a garment, the stretchy part is an extravagance, forbidden to be spoken of

definitions.text: In a garment, the stretchy part

indicators.note: spoken of means the words are heard rather than read, so go by sound

parts.note: waste, spending without need, sounds like the body's middle
banned means forbidden

explanation.surface: A clothing item's elastic part is too lavish to mention.
explanation.definitionFit: The waistband of trousers or a skirt is often elasticated, making it the part of the garment that stretches.

clue.text: I'm past a developmental phase

parts.note: taken as written
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Someone saying they have grown out of a phase.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final, adult stage in an insect's development, after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Professional organization led by one of its members into an intense situation

parts.note: a doctor belongs to a medical association
the AMA is the American Medical Association

explanation.surface: A professional body led by one of its own into a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led by' puts the member in front; the member must be a doctor because the body is the American Medical Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama, as in workplace drama, is an informal word for an emotionally charged situation.

clue.text: Strange moon lander returning less than halfway

indicators.note: returning means going back, so read the letters in the opposite direction
stopping before the halfway mark means most of the name is dropped, keeping only an opening run

parts.note: Neil Armstrong was the first person to land on the moon

explanation.surface: Something odd about an astronaut who turned back before getting halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep NEILA, five of the astronaut's thirteen letters and so under half, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means foreign or unfamiliar, just as strange does.

clue.text: Citadel is stormed, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: a stormed fortress is overrun and wrecked, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fortress attacked, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a stock phrase meaning 'so to speak'; only 'manner of speaking' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, a particular way people talk.

clue.text: Paint the housekeeper on The Brady Bunch, almost suppressing sob

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the name loses its final letter
suppressing something means holding it down inside, so one word is enclosed by the other

parts.words: the housekeeper on The Brady Bunch
parts.note: Alice Nelson was the Bradys' housekeeper, cut short by one letter
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: Alice from the sitcom holding back tears while she paints.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brady Bunch was a 1970s US sitcom whose housekeeper was Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a quick-drying synthetic paint used by artists and decorators.

clue.text: New England city and state with a piece of land that brought the death of 1-Across

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the event

parts.note: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts
Mass. is the abbreviation for Massachusetts
an acre is a measured plot of land

explanation.surface: A place in New England whose land saw a famous death.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1770 Boston Massacre, when British troops fired on a crowd, killed Crispus Attucks among others.
explanation.definitionFit: The massacre was the incident in which Attucks was shot, the event that caused his death.
